reason: The cited evidence (E1–E4) does not directly support the key premises. E1 discusses nanoindentation creep of Al-containing HEAs, E2 describes fusion reactor requirements, E3 lists refractory HEA compositions and properties but not WTaTiVZr, and E4 reports nanoindentation creep of HfTaTiVZr and TaTiVWZr at low temperatures (298–573 K). None of the passages provide evidence for lattice distortions, Peierls barrier reduction, or enhanced dislocation mobility in WTaTiVZr at high temperatures.
premises: WTaTiVZr is a homogeneous equimolar BCC solid solution
Multi-element composition induces significant lattice distortions
Lattice distortions lower the Peierls barrier for dislocation nucleation and mobility
Lowered Peierls barrier promotes dynamic recovery and delays crack initiation
This mechanism enhances plastic strain and toughness relative to pure tungsten at high temperature
